title: FEZE: Alignment-Flexible Zero-Shot Vertical Federated Learning

problem.claim: Zero-shot vertical federated learning must recognize test classes that are absent from some or all parties' training data, sometimes with no aligned training samples.

gap.claim: Existing zero-shot methods require abundant seen-class samples, while ZVFL faces limited aligned samples, heterogeneous seen-class distributions, insufficient seen-to-unseen transfer, and inconsistent multi-party prediction bias.

contributions.claim: FEZE is an alignment-flexible zero-shot vertical federated learning framework.
A relation learning network and meta-relation learning mechanism model class-feature relationships and improve feature generalization from limited seen-class samples.
An alignment-flexible adaptive aggregation strategy aggregates inconsistent prediction spaces with an arbitrary number of aligned samples.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Theoretical analysis reports a convergence rate of O(1/T).
In the zero-shot setting without aligned samples, FEZE reportedly surpasses state-of-the-art baselines by an average of 7.47% across three datasets.

narrative_sequence.summary: The paper frames zero-shot vertical federated learning as a setting where test classes may be absent from parties' training data.
It identifies limited aligned samples, heterogeneous seen classes, weak transfer, and inconsistent party bias as core challenges.
FEZE addresses the challenges with relation learning, meta-relation learning, and alignment-flexible adaptive aggregation.
The abstract reports a convergence rate and performance improvement in the no-alignment setting.

unknowns: The abstract does not identify the three datasets or baselines.
The abstract does not provide experimental protocols, variance, statistical tests, or implementation details.
The assumptions and proof details behind the reported convergence rate are unspecified.
